 NFC Notes: Budda Baker, Sam Darnold, 49ers, Cardinals, Seahawks
 By Wyatt Grindley - October 19, 2026 
 49ers 
 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan praised WR Jordan  Watkins ‘ recent performance after several injuries have hit the receiving corps, forcing the next man up into the lineup .
 “We’ve been really happy with how he’s played in these games,” Shanahan said, via Niners Wire . “I think he’s earned a lot of respect in these three games and with us, it doesn’t have to do with the stats. I know he’s had two catches and stuff in his first game, and those are two really good plays, but because he hasn’t had any in the other two games doesn’t really mean much to us.” 
 Shanahan added: “If the ball’s supposed to go to him, he’s supposed to do his job and we expect him to come through with that, but he’s done his job in all these plays. He’s blocked well, he’s run good routes, he’s gotten open. We’ve been really happy with how he’s stepped up in these few games.” 
 49ers WR Mike Evans was asked why he left Tampa Bay for San Francisco this offseason: “This team rejuvenated me and probably added a few more years to my career… They had everything I needed and checked every box. They’re trying to win now. The quarterback, great skill players, great defense, great coaching staff, and lastly, a great organization.” ( Rick Stroud )
 Cardinals 
 Heat was building on Cardinals DC  Nick Rallis as Arizona limped to a 1-4 start to the season. But defensive players were quick to point to Rallis as a big reason the team pulled off an 18-16 upset over the Rams in Week 6. 
 “He had a great defensive plan,” Cardinals S Budda Baker said via Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer . “Throughout the week, he told us, how he saw things, how he was going to call it. And that’s exactly how he called it. So shout-out to Nick. And whether he had some conversations with [head coach Mike] LaFleur or not, I think he definitely did a great job of the game plan. And we just tried to execute it. So shout-out Nick. Shout-out defensive coaches on the plan this week.” 
 Seahawks 
 Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald said the team isn’t considering making any quarterback changes after questions have risen about QB Sam Darnold ‘s performance so far in 2026.
 “I think we have a lot of faith in Sam,” Macdonald said, via ESPN . “Sam’s played great football for us. He’s done a lot of great things this year but obviously turned the ball over more than we want to. I feel like there’s things on our end that can help him play better football, and I think he’s definitely part of the solution rather than the opposite.”
